newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge to third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge to third straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks powered to a record close for the third day in a row on Wednesday, as fundamental and technical factors combined to keep bulls buying blue chips in the market, traders and analysts said.
"It is amazing, the market rallied on the back of heavyweights Telmex and Televisa, which gave a huge pyschological boost, too," a trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX closed up 41.84 points, or 1.19 percent, at 3,557.97.
Telecommunications firm Telmex and media group Televisa gained 46 centavos and 5.90 pesos, respectively, to 14.78 and 108.30 pesos. Their ADRs meanwhile both ended up 1-1/2, at 37-3/4 and 27-3/4.

"Bullish blue chips are a hallmark of this rally. Televisa in particular has been favored by an expected operating improvement and lower indebtedness now its separation from Panamsat has been finalized," said Roberto Galvan, equity analyst at the Bursamtrica consultancy firm.
Analysts said the rally was also fueled by falls in primary interest rates and forecast economic growth.
Several analysts said market fundamentals could sustain the rally for several more sessions.

"The Bolsa looks firm to me. January is always a good month as foreign investors acquire positions for the year. The rally could last at least another three weeks and take us towards a target of 3,600 where it might rest," said Alexander Anderson, an analyst with the Abaco brokerage.
Volume .TV.MX improved over recent sessions to 109.3 million shares traded, which included several hefty cross trades, but still reflected interest among foreign investors.
Some notes of caution were sounded concerning the short-term prospects for the current rally to continue, however.
"This rally has been basically Telmex-led," said Ramon Ruiz, sales trader at the Latam equities desk with Bankers Trust in New York.
"Telmex ADRs broke resistance again today, so they can either head for 40 or slow down," Ruiz said.
"Apart from today, I've seen little volume in Mexico to match New York, so I think it'll slow down, which would mean the Bolsa will accumulate in its new trading range," he added.
On the broad market, meanwhile, 101 shares changed hands, of which gains outnumbered sliders by 49 to 38.
Food company Herdez headed the gains PG.MX., up 23 centavos to 2.43 pesos.
"It's a fairly illiquid stock that had lagged behind the market, but could have been in demand as its sector has a better outlook this year," a broker said.
Beverage firm Emvasa was in second place, up 28 centavos to 4.68 pesos, on news it was to sell a $15 million stake in another company.
Debt-ridden holding company headed the falls, off 16 centavos to 80 centavos, albeit at thin volume.
Most heavily traded slider was financial group GFB, off one centavo at 3.12 pesos.
((--Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
